Every case's 'question' is the EXACT literal text a corpus runner must send to address it -- routing is by a normalized hash of this text (provider_scripts.question_fingerprint), never a marker embedded in the question (see provider_scripts.py's module docstring for why). Phase 2 Lane 2b case authors add more entries here as they author tests/acceptance/world/ask-dev-world.v1/corpus/case-*.json, pinning each case's own real question text; an id present in registry-ids.v1.json but absent from this file's 'cases' is simply not addressable yet -- a question that doesn't match any entry here falls through to the untagged default heuristic exactly like any other ordinary question, so under-coverage never masks as false success (see registry-ids.v1.json cross-check conformance tests).

decisions.prompt: Which project named "Atlas" did you mean?

pers.clarification-persistence.comment: CHAOS-3577 (2026-08-07): was kind=delegate_default, which made this case prove the OPPOSITE of its name. Its profile expects needs_clarification, but with the engine live delegate_default fell through to the unscripted widen-and-disclose heuristic and the measured armed run recorded answered_with_gaps -- a clarification-PERSISTENCE case that never clarified. It now carries the same disambiguation SHAPE as scope.ambiguous, which orchestrator.py maps to needs_clarification unconditionally, so the case exercises the mechanism it is named for and its existing profile expectation becomes satisfiable without changing it. The QUESTION IS DELIBERATELY ITS OWN and not copied from scope.ambiguous: role_script_identity_digest keys on by_fingerprint and test_ask_dev_provider_roles asserts len(by_fingerprint) == len(cases), so two entries sharing a question would collide their fingerprint and fail. Candidates mirror scope.ambiguous's (atlas/api, atlas/web); no prompt text or candidate list is pinned anywhere, so they are chosen to match the sibling rather than invented differently.
